name: Iron deficiency anaemia
cap: Iron deficiency: microcytic hypochromic red cells with pencil cells; a small lymphocyte gives the scale.

name: Dimorphic picture
cap: Dimorphic picture: small pale red cells mixed with normal ones, as in sideroblastic anaemia or treated iron deficiency.

name: Ring sideroblasts
cap: Ring sideroblasts (arrows): Perls-positive granules encircling the nucleus of erythroblasts.

name: Marrow iron stores (Perls)
cap: Perls stain of marrow: blue haemosiderin in macrophages, showing that iron stores are present.

name: Increased marrow iron (Perls)
cap: Perls stain of a marrow fragment with abundant blue iron, as in iron overload or anaemia of chronic disorders.

name: Macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophil
cap: Oval macrocytes and a hypersegmented neutrophil: the classic megaloblastic pair.

name: Howell–Jolly bodies
cap: Howell–Jolly bodies (arrows): nuclear remnants left behind by megaloblastic red cells.

name: Cabot ring
cap: Cabot ring (arrow): a loop-shaped remnant of the mitotic spindle.

name: Megaloblastic marrow
cap: Megaloblastic marrow: large erythroid precursors with open, finely stippled chromatin.

name: Giant metamyelocytes
cap: Giant metamyelocytes and bands: they persist for a while after treatment.

name: β thalassaemia major
cap: β thalassaemia major: marked anisopoikilocytosis with inclusion-laden cells.

name: Thalassaemia after splenectomy
cap: Thalassaemia after splenectomy: target cells, Howell–Jolly bodies, spherocytes and nucleated red cells (NRC).

name: HbH inclusions
cap: HbH inclusions: brilliant cresyl blue gives the even, golf-ball stippling of HbH disease.

name: Sickle cells
cap: Sickle cells and target cells in sickle cell anaemia.

name: Positive sickling test
cap: Positive sickling test: red cells sickle under a sealed coverslip with a reducing agent.

name: HbS solubility test
cap: HbS solubility test: turbid patient tubes hide the lines, compared with positive and negative controls.

name: HbC crystals
cap: HbC crystals (arrows) inside red cells.

name: Haemoglobin electrophoresis gels
cap: Alkaline and acid gels: HbS and HbC separate from D, G, E and A₂ only on the acid gel.

name: Hereditary spherocytosis
cap: Hereditary spherocytosis: small dense spherocytes without central pallor, and polychromatic cells.

name: Hereditary elliptocytosis
cap: Hereditary elliptocytosis: most cells are elliptical (arrows).

name: Stomatocytes
cap: Stomatocytes: a slit-like, mouth-shaped central pallor.

name: Acanthocytes
cap: Acanthocytes: dense cells with a few irregular spiky projections.

name: Osmotic fragility test
cap: Osmotic fragility tubes: in hereditary spherocytosis lysis starts at higher saline concentrations than normal.

name: SDS-PAGE of membrane proteins
cap: SDS-PAGE of red cell membrane proteins: spectrins, ankyrin, band 3, 4.1 and 4.2.

name: Bite and blister cells (G6PD)
cap: G6PD haemolysis: bite cells (arrows) and blister cells (arrowheads).

name: Heinz bodies
cap: Heinz bodies: precipitated oxidised haemoglobin on a supravital stain.

name: G6PD fluorescent spot test
cap: Fluorescent spot test: normal samples glow under UV; G6PD-deficient spots stay dark.

name: Pyruvate kinase deficiency (echinocytes)
cap: Pyruvate kinase deficiency: echinocytes with short regular spicules (arrow).

name: Spherocytes (warm AIHA)
cap: Warm AIHA: spherocytes (arrows) and polychromasia.

name: Red cell agglutination (cold agglutinins)
cap: Cold agglutinin disease: red cells clumped together on a film made at room temperature.

name: Schistocytes
cap: Microangiopathic haemolysis: schistocytes (helmet cells and fragments).

name: Ham test
cap: Ham test: patient (Pt) cells lyse in acidified serum at 37 °C, control (C) cells do not.

name: PNH flow cytometry (CD59)
cap: PNH flow cytometry: red cells with normal, partial (type II) and absent (type III) CD59.

name: Haematuria versus haemoglobinuria
cap: Dark urine: red cells settle on centrifugation (haematuria), haemoglobin stays in solution (haemoglobinuria).

name: Principle of the Ham test
cap: Principle of the Ham test: PNH cells lacking CD55 and CD59 are lysed by complement in acidified serum.

name: CML, chronic phase
cap: CML, chronic phase: granulocytes at every stage, with myelocytes and a basophil.

name: CML marrow
cap: CML marrow: packed with granulocytic precursors; erythroid cells are few.

name: Pseudo-Gaucher cell
cap: Pseudo-Gaucher cell in CML: a macrophage with striated blue cytoplasm.

name: Chronic neutrophilic leukaemia
cap: Chronic neutrophilic leukaemia: mature segmented neutrophils dominate; precursors are few.

name: Polycythaemia vera
cap: Polycythaemia vera: crowded red cells with a raised neutrophil and platelet count.

name: Essential thrombocythaemia
cap: Essential thrombocythaemia: many platelets of varying size.

name: Large megakaryocyte with staghorn nucleus
cap: ET marrow: a giant megakaryocyte with a deeply lobulated, staghorn nucleus.

name: Teardrop cells (myelofibrosis)
cap: Primary myelofibrosis: teardrop cells with a nucleated red cell and a myelocyte (leucoerythroblastic picture).

name: Atypical megakaryocyte clusters (PMF)
cap: PMF trephine: dense clusters of atypical megakaryocytes.

name: Reticulin fibrosis
cap: Reticulin stain: an increased network of reticulin fibres.

name: Collagen fibrosis (trichrome)
cap: Trichrome stain: collagen fibrosis (blue) between bony trabeculae in advanced myelofibrosis.

name: Chronic eosinophilic leukaemia
cap: Chronic eosinophilic leukaemia: sheets of eosinophils and their precursors.

name: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia
cap: JMML: monocytes and immature myeloid cells in a child's blood.

name: Spindle mast cell infiltrate (SM)
cap: Systemic mastocytosis trephine: a dense infiltrate of spindle-shaped mast cells (arrows).

name: Atypical spindle mast cell
cap: Atypical type I mast cell (arrow): spindle shape, oval central nucleus and hypogranular cytoplasm.

name: Mast cells in marrow aspirate
cap: Marrow aspirate in systemic mastocytosis: granulated mast cells (arrows) among myeloid precursors.

name: Promastocyte
cap: Promastocyte (atypical type II): a bilobed nucleus, a sign of aggressive disease.

name: Tryptase-positive mast cell aggregate
cap: Tryptase immunostain of the trephine: a dense mast cell aggregate, the major criterion.

name: Mast cell leukaemia (blood)
cap: Mast cell leukaemia: round mast cells packed with dark metachromatic granules.

name: Mast cell leukaemia trephine
cap: Mast cell leukaemia trephine: diffuse, dense sheets of mast cells efface the marrow.

name: MDS blood film
cap: MDS blood film: anisopoikilocytosis with ovalocytes and teardrop cells, and dysplastic neutrophils.

name: Pseudo-Pelger–Huët neutrophils
cap: Dysgranulopoiesis: hyposegmented, hypogranular neutrophils (pseudo-Pelger–Huët).

name: Dysgranulopoiesis
cap: Dysgranulopoiesis: a hypogranular neutrophil, a ring-shaped nucleus and a bilobed pseudo-Pelger cell.

name: Dyserythropoiesis: multinucleate erythroblasts
cap: Dyserythropoiesis: binucleate and multinucleate erythroblasts, nuclear budding and irregular nuclei.

name: Dyserythropoiesis: vacuoles and karyorrhexis
cap: More dyserythropoiesis: cytoplasmic vacuoles, karyorrhexis and megaloblastoid nuclei.

name: Myeloblasts in MDS
cap: Myeloblasts in MDS with increased blasts: large cells with fine chromatin.

name: Dysplastic megakaryocytes
cap: Dysmegakaryopoiesis in an MDS aspirate: abnormal megakaryocytes with separated nuclei.

name: Micromegakaryocyte
cap: Micromegakaryocyte: a small megakaryocyte with a single round nucleus, the most reliable dysplastic sign.

name: MDS trephine
cap: MDS trephine: hypercellular marrow with dysplastic, hypolobated megakaryocytes.

name: CD34+ blast cluster (ALIP)
cap: CD34 immunostain: a cluster of blasts away from the trabeculae (ALIP).

name: CMML blood film
cap: CMML blood film: many monocytes with folded nuclei and grey cytoplasm, mixed with neutrophils.

name: CMML: abnormal monocytes
cap: CMML blood film: mature and abnormal monocytes with a dysplastic neutrophil.

name: CMML marrow aspirate
cap: CMML marrow aspirate: granulocytic and monocytic hyperplasia with left shift.

name: CMML trephine
cap: CMML trephine: hypercellular marrow with myelomonocytic proliferation.

name: CMML trephine, high power
cap: CMML trephine at higher power: a dysplastic megakaryocyte among myelomonocytic cells.

name: Double esterase stain in CMML
cap: Double esterase stain: monocytic cells stain red-brown (non-specific esterase), granulocytes blue (chloroacetate esterase).

name: Monocytic immunostain in CMML
cap: Immunohistochemistry for a monocytic marker (CD14/CD163): many brown-staining monocytes in CMML marrow.

name: CD123+ plasmacytoid dendritic cell nodule
cap: CD123 immunostain: a nodule of plasmacytoid dendritic cells, seen in about 20% of CMML.

name: MDS/MPN with neutrophilia: blood film
cap: MDS/MPN with neutrophilia: leucocytosis with immature granulocytes and dysplastic, hypogranular neutrophils.

name: MDS/MPN with neutrophilia: trephine
cap: MDS/MPN with neutrophilia trephine: hypercellular with granulocytic predominance (M:E >10 : 1).

name: MDS/MPN-SF3B1-T trephine
cap: MDS/MPN-SF3B1-T trephine: large MPN-like megakaryocytes in a hypercellular marrow.

name: Ring sideroblasts in MDS/MPN-SF3B1-T
cap: Perls stain in MDS/MPN-SF3B1-T: ring sideroblasts with blue iron granules around the nucleus.

name: Myeloblast
cap: Myeloblast: a large cell with fine chromatin, nucleoli and basophilic, agranular cytoplasm.

name: Monoblast
cap: Monoblast: the largest blast, with a round nucleus, lacy chromatin and abundant grey-blue cytoplasm.

name: AML aspirate, low power
cap: AML marrow aspirate at low power: a particle packed with blasts.

name: AML marrow aspirate
cap: AML marrow aspirate: sheets of blasts replace the normal series.

name: AML trephine
cap: AML trephine: hypercellular marrow effaced by blasts.

name: AML with minimal differentiation (M0)
cap: AML with minimal differentiation (M0): an agranular blast with no Auer rods; myeloid only by flow cytometry.

name: AML without maturation (M1)
cap: AML without maturation (M1): uniform blasts with scanty granules and few maturing cells.

name: AML with maturation (M2)
cap: AML with maturation (M2): blasts with granules alongside maturing granulocytes.

name: Hypergranular APL (M3)
cap: Hypergranular APL (M3): promyelocytes packed with coarse granules that obscure the nucleus.

name: APL faggot cell
cap: APL faggot cell (arrow): a bundle of Auer rods in the cytoplasm.

name: Microgranular APL (M3v)
cap: Microgranular APL (M3v): bilobed, butterfly-shaped nuclei and apparently agranular cytoplasm.

name: Acute myelomonocytic leukaemia (M4)
cap: Acute myelomonocytic leukaemia (M4): myeloblasts with monoblasts and promonocytes.

name: M4Eo: abnormal eosinophils
cap: M4Eo: abnormal eosinophils with coarse purple-red granules among myelomonocytic blasts.

name: AML with CBFB::MYH11
cap: AML with CBFB::MYH11: myelomonocytic blasts with immature eosinophils carrying large dark granules.

name: Double esterase stain in AML
cap: Double esterase stain: monocytic cells stain dark blue, neutrophil precursors reddish-brown.

name: Acute monoblastic leukaemia (M5a)
cap: Acute monoblastic leukaemia (M5a): large monoblasts with round nuclei, nucleoli and abundant blue cytoplasm.

name: Acute monocytic leukaemia (M5b)
cap: Acute monocytic leukaemia (M5b): promonocytes and monocytes with folded nuclei.

name: Erythroleukaemia (M6)
cap: Erythroleukaemia (M6): deeply basophilic, vacuolated proerythroblasts with dysplastic erythroblasts.

name: Acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia (M7)
cap: Acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia (M7): blasts with cytoplasmic blebs.

name: Hairy cells in blood
cap: Hairy cells in the blood: oval nuclei, ground-glass chromatin and pale cytoplasm with circumferential projections.

name: Hairy cell, electron micrograph
cap: Electron micrograph of a hairy cell: long cytoplasmic villi all around the cell.

name: HCL trephine: fried-egg cells
cap: HCL trephine: fried-egg cells with clear cytoplasm and sharp cell borders (arrow).

name: HCL trephine
cap: HCL trephine: interstitial infiltrate with preserved fat and haemopoiesis.

name: Rouleaux in myeloma
cap: Rouleaux: red cells stacked like coins by the high protein.

name: Urine electrophoresis: M spike
cap: Urine electrophoresis with a monoclonal (M) spike of light chains.

name: Serum immunofixation
cap: Immunofixation: the band reacts with one heavy chain antiserum and one light chain.

name: Myeloma plasma cells
cap: Myeloma plasma cells: eccentric nuclei, clock-face chromatin and a perinuclear hof.

name: Lymphoplasmacytoid myeloma cell
cap: Lymphoplasmacytoid (small-cell) myeloma cell.

name: Malignant plasmablast
cap: Malignant plasmablast: dispersed chromatin and a prominent nucleolus (adverse).

name: Multinucleated plasma cell
cap: Multinucleated plasma cell.

name: Mott cell
cap: Mott cell: cytoplasm packed with Russell bodies (immunoglobulin).

name: Flame cell
cap: Flame cell: red-fringed cytoplasm, typical of IgA myeloma.

name: Pseudo-Gaucher cells in myeloma
cap: Pseudo-Gaucher change: plasma cells stuffed with fibrillary material.

name: Crystalline rods in plasma cells
cap: Crystalline rods in plasma cell cytoplasm.

name: Forward vs side scatter plot
cap: Forward against side scatter: lymphocytes low on both, monocytes in the middle, granulocytes high side scatter.

name: Gating on forward scatter
cap: Gate R1 drawn around lymphocytes on a forward/side scatter plot; the line shows debris excluded by the threshold.

name: Sequential gating
cap: Sequential gating: lymphocytes on CD45/SSC, then CD2+CD20− T cells, then CD2+CD8+ cells.

name: Flow histogram: negative and positive peaks
cap: Histogram: region M1 covers the negative peak and M2 the positive peak.

name: CD4 histogram
cap: CD4 histogram with a small negative population on the left and a bright positive peak.

name: Antibody titration histograms
cap: Antibody titration: the positive peak moves right as the antibody becomes more concentrated (1/40 to 1/5); the blue line marks the unstained level.

name: Density plot
cap: Density plot with contour lines: colour shows where events are crowded.

name: Contour plot
cap: Contour diagram of blood: lymphocytes, monocytes and granulocytes as separate peaks, like a survey map.

name: CD45/SSC: myeloblasts
cap: CD45/SSC: myeloblasts in the blast gate (dim CD45, low side scatter).

name: CD45/SSC: neoplastic promyelocytes
cap: CD45/SSC in APL: neoplastic promyelocytes with high side scatter.

name: CD45/SSC: hypogranular APL
cap: CD45/SSC in hypogranular APL: the cells fall lower, because the granules are submicroscopic.

name: CD45/SSC: monoblasts
cap: CD45/SSC: monoblasts with moderate CD45 and higher side scatter.

name: CD34/CD45 in acute leukaemia
cap: CD34 against CD45 in acute leukaemia: the arrow marks CD34+ blasts with dim CD45.

name: CD11b/CD15 in AML with inv(16)
cap: AML with inv(16): CD11b against CD15 shows several populations with asynchronous maturation.

name: CD33/CD34 in AML with t(9;11)
cap: AML with t(9;11): blasts (red) bright CD33 with little CD34.

name: CD41 on megakaryoblasts
cap: Megakaryoblastic AML: blasts (red) express CD41; blue and green are reference populations.

name: B-ALL: HLA-DR/CD34
cap: B-ALL: blasts (red) HLA-DR+ and CD34+.

name: B-ALL: CD10/CD34
cap: B-ALL: blasts (red) CD10 bright with CD34.

name: B-ALL: cyCD79a/TdT
cap: B-ALL: cytoplasmic CD79a and TdT positive.

name: B-ALL: CD13/CD117
cap: B-ALL: blasts negative for CD13 and CD117 (no myeloid commitment).

name: MPAL B/myeloid: CD79a/MPO
cap: MPAL B/myeloid: one population carries both cytoplasmic CD79a and MPO.

name: MPAL T/myeloid: cCD3/MPO
cap: MPAL T/myeloid: separate populations positive for cytoplasmic CD3 (green) and for MPO (red).

name: Plasma cell gate on CD45/SSC
cap: Gating possible plasma cells (green) in the CD45-negative region.

name: Plasma cells: kappa restriction
cap: Plasma cells: no surface light chain but intracellular κ restriction.

name: Myeloma: CD45−CD56+
cap: Myeloma cells (red): CD45 negative and CD56 positive.

name: Plasma cells: CD38 bright, CD20−
cap: Plasma cells (red): CD38 bright and CD20 negative; blue dots are normal B cells.

name: Lambda light-chain restriction
cap: λ light-chain restriction: 79% of CD19/CD20+ B cells are λ positive.

name: Burkitt lymphoma: high forward scatter
cap: Burkitt lymphoma: large lymphoid cells with high forward scatter (green) above normal small lymphocytes.

name: Burkitt lymphoma: CD20+ CD5−
cap: Burkitt lymphoma: CD20 bright, CD5 negative B cells.

name: Hairy cells on CD45/SSC
cap: Hairy cell leukaemia: atypical lymphocytes with bright CD45 and slightly raised side scatter.

name: T-cell lymphoma: CD7 loss
cap: T-cell lymphoma: tumour cells lose CD3 while benign T cells keep CD3 and CD7.

name: Basophils in AML with t(6;9)
cap: AML with t(6;9): increased marrow basophils beside blasts.

name: Cup-like blasts in NPM1-mutated AML
cap: AML with mutated NPM1: blasts with cup-like nuclear invaginations.

name: Megakaryoblasts with blebs
cap: Acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia: blasts with cytoplasmic blebs.

name: B lymphoblasts
cap: B lymphoblasts: high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio and fine chromatin.

name: Megakaryocyte with platelets
cap: Megakaryocyte surrounded by masses of aggregated platelets (marrow aspirate).

name: Increased platelets
cap: Peripheral blood film with increased platelets of varying size among normal red cells.

name: Large platelets (anisocytosis)
cap: Platelet anisocytosis: tiny to large forms beside a megakaryocyte fragment.

name: Marrow particle with megakaryocytes
cap: Marrow particle with several megakaryocytes between fat spaces.

name: Megakaryocytes on trephine
cap: Trephine biopsy (H&E) showing clustered, large megakaryocytes.
